A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAM study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, experimental appendices and proofs are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original CIFAR-10/100 experiments on late- and early-phase SAM, ASAM and adversarial training, alongside toy-model simulations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds original experiments involving vision transformers, squared loss, USAM, sharpness dynamics and perturbation-radius sensitivity in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The practical SAM update and epoch-based switching procedure are retained. The independent inner/outer mini-batches made explicit in v2 Equation (4) were already assumed in v1 Appendix B. The additional optimizer studies extend evaluation of the switching approach.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10/100 classification, adversarial evaluation and the same toy problem. V2's transformers, squared-loss experiments and 5,000-example CIFAR-10 subset change configurations or sample sizes, without introducing a new dataset population or task.

E2.justification: V2 substantially broadens the optimizer comparisons: Figure 8 includes Adam-based training, described as AdamW in B.1; Figure 11 compares switched USAM with full USAM; and Figure 13 includes full-batch GD and SAM controls. The original SGD, SAM, ASAM and adversarial-training comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Added protocols include ViT-T/S training with AdamW, AutoAugment and batch size 64; squared-loss VGG-16/19 experiments reporting Frobenius-norm sharpness; and full-batch sharpness tracking on a 5,000-example subset with learning rate 0.01. V2 also adds a five-value perturbation-radius sweep and two-dimensional landscape sampling. These supplement the retained original protocols.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests connecting experiments to the theory's squared-loss and unnormalized-SAM assumptions, an early-SAM edge-of-stability analysis, perturbation-radius sensitivity, two-dimensional valley visualizations and longer escape/convergence trajectories (Figures 9, 11 and 13–16). These investigate questions beyond v1's existing switching and interpolation analyses.

E5.justification: Matched experiments retain their three- or five-trial mean/standard-deviation reporting and the 100-trial escape trajectories. Added experiments reuse these reporting practices. No new confidence-interval procedure, significance test or explicit increase in repeated runs for retained experiments is reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for transformers, squared loss, USAM, GD sharpness evolution, radius sensitivity and landscape/dynamics analyses. New findings include sharpness approaching the GD stability threshold after switching from SAM and little radius-dependent variation after subsequent SGD training. Figure 4(b) also reports different escape-loss trajectories. These are additional or revised results, rather than demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 revises proof updates to take the outer step from the original parameter rather than the perturbed point and rewrites the convergence derivation. Proposition 4.1 adds the restriction rho ≤ eta; Theorem 4.3 tightens the respective smoothness-based step limits from 1/L to 1/(2L) and 1/(4L). Appendix C adds conditional-expectation reasoning, a multiple-valley example and Proposition C.2 extending the initialization range.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: late-phase SAM efficiently finds flatter solutions, its dynamics admit an escape/convergence picture, late optimization strongly influences final properties, and analogous behavior occurs with adversarial training. Additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly confines the exponential-escape interpretation to the local linear regime and clarifies that near-tightness of the SGD sharpness bound is empirical. It interprets the new GD and radius studies as further evidence for late-optimizer dominance and explains why transformer sharpness measurements are omitted. The original limitations paragraph remains substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: V1 describes supplementary code and planned checkpoint release; v2 reports a public source-code repository. V2 also documents USAM's perturbation radius, transformer training hyperparameters and augmentation, and the sampling/normalization procedure for two-dimensional landscape plots.

R1.justification: V2 expands the retained related-work discussion with normalization, decentralized SGD, gradient regularization and Jia and Su's related late-training regularizer, among other citations. These additions improve contextual coverage while retaining the paper's positioning around late-phase SAM dynamics.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Section 2 to Appendix A, with subsequent sections and appendices renumbered. V2 clarifies notation, condenses repeated explanations and captions, and edits language and publication information. Most of the main narrative and prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adds seven figures covering the new experiments, contour views and extended dynamics. Existing ASAM and early-SAM figures are retained as Figures 10 and 12; captions and placement are revised, and Figure 4(b)'s axes and plotted trajectories change. Some new labeling is inconsistent: Figure 13's caption reverses the switching direction shown in its legend and discussion.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through targeted squared-loss, USAM, sharpness-dynamics and sensitivity checks, and improves documentation and research context. Its proof revisions address v1's inconsistent outer-update origin. However, the rewritten convergence derivation in C.3.1 contains a gradient-norm bound inconsistent with Lemma C.1, so the theoretical repair remains incomplete. The empirical and transparency gains support a positive but limited overall improvement.
